quick: Apply a small volume of 0.06% (capsule) or 0.15% (membrane) solution intraocularly
Negligible systemic exposure; use as needed during surgery
Remove all excess dye; inspect for lens/structure staining
summary: Trypan blue is a sterile ophthalmic solution used during eye surgery as a selective tissue stain. The 0.06% strength (e.g., VisionBlue) stains the anterior lens capsule to aid capsulorhexis during cataract surgery, while the 0.15% strength (e.g., MembraneBlue) stains epiretinal and internal limiting membranes during vitrectomy. It is applied directly to the target tissue inside the eye and all excess dye must be removed. It is not a systemic medicine; systemic absorption from intraocular use is negligible.
indications: Selective staining of the anterior lens capsule during cataract surgery to aid visualization for capsulorhexis (0.06% solution)
Selective staining of epiretinal membranes and the internal limiting membrane during vitrectomy surgery (0.15% solution)

dosage.d: Inject a small amount of 0.06% solution onto the anterior lens capsule under air or viscoelastic
dosage.n: Remove excess dye and air; rinse anterior chamber

dosage.d: Apply 0.15% solution to the membrane via blunt cannula after fluid-air exchange, or inject into BSS-filled cavity and wait ~30 seconds
dosage.n: Remove all excess dye from the vitreous cavity before completing surgery

admin: For intraocular ophthalmic use by an ophthalmic surgeon only
Apply directly to the target tissue (anterior capsule or retinal membrane) under sterile technique
For ILM/epiretinal staining, perform a fluid-air exchange first or inject into a BSS-filled cavity and allow ~30 seconds of contact
Aspirate and remove all excess dye from the eye immediately after staining
Do not use with non-hydrated (dry) hydrophilic acrylic intraocular lenses, which can absorb the dye
moa: Trypan blue is an acid diazo dye that selectively binds to and stains cellular and basement-membrane structures with a high affinity for non-viable or collagen-containing tissues. In the eye this produces contrast that highlights the anterior lens capsule and the epiretinal/internal limiting membranes, allowing the surgeon to better visualize and manipulate these otherwise transparent structures during surgery. It has no pharmacologic systemic action when used intraocularly.

absolute: Insertion of a non-hydrated (dry-state) hydrophilic acrylic intraocular lens, which may absorb the dye and become discolored
monitor: Inadvertent staining of the posterior capsule or vitreous face

preg: Systemic absorption from a single small intraocular application is negligible, and reproductive risk to the fetus is not expected. Use during pregnancy as required for surgery.
lact: Because systemic absorption from intraocular surgical use is negligible, trypan blue is not expected to be present in breast milk in clinically relevant amounts and is considered compatible with breastfeeding.
renal: Not applicable - trypan blue is used topically inside the eye during surgery with negligible systemic absorption; no renal dose adjustment is required.
hepatic: Not applicable - trypan blue is used topically inside the eye during surgery with negligible systemic absorption; no hepatic dose adjustment is required.

major: None known for intraocular surgical use
minor: May be absorbed by certain hydrophilic intraocular lens materials, causing lens discoloration
interactions.diagnostics: No systemic laboratory interference; can transiently tint ocular tissues and any retained dye is visible intraoperatively.

common: Transient staining of intraocular structures (expected effect)
serious: Inadvertent staining of the posterior lens capsule and vitreous face
Discoloration of high-water-content hydrogel intraocular lenses
rare: Corneal endothelial effects with excessive exposure

monitoring: Intraoperative confirmation that excess dye is fully removed
Inspection of the intraocular lens for unintended discoloration
Assessment of staining adequacy of the target tissue
Postoperative monitoring of vision recovery (transient tissue staining usually resolves within about one week)
counsel: This is a surgical dye applied by your eye surgeon during the operation, not a medicine you take
Any temporary staining of eye tissues generally clears within about a week
Report any unusual or persistent vision changes after surgery
Tell your surgeon about prior reactions to dyes used in eye procedures
pk: Stains tissue within seconds of contact
Tissue tint typically resolves within about 1 week
Store at 15-25 C (59-77 F); protect from direct sunlight
pearls: Two strengths: 0.06% for anterior capsule (cataract) staining and 0.15% for retinal membrane (vitrectomy) staining
Always remove ALL excess dye from the eye after staining
Avoid with dry hydrophilic acrylic IOLs - the lens can absorb and retain the dye
Improves visualization of the capsulorhexis in mature/white cataracts with poor red reflex
Not a systemic drug - no organ-based dose adjustments apply
missed: Not applicable - trypan blue is administered once intraoperatively by the surgeon and is not a self-administered or scheduled medication.
overdose: Overdose is not a relevant concern for intraocular surgical use; only small volumes are applied and excess is removed during surgery. Excessive intraocular dye should be aspirated and the eye irrigated. Systemic toxicity from ophthalmic use is not expected.
